html:
Butrint is an ancient city on a lake near the southern tip of Albania, facing Corfu, inhabited from the Greek period through Roman, Byzantine and Venetian times until it was abandoned in the late Middle Ages.

Legend said it was founded by Trojan exiles. It grew around a sanctuary of Asclepius, the god of healing, and had a theatre by the 200s BCE. Under Augustus it became a Roman colony with an aqueduct, baths and a forum. A large baptistery with floor mosaics dates from the 500s. Venice held it as an outpost for centuries, and its marshes later made it unhealthy. Excavated since the 1920s, it is a World Heritage Site and the best known ancient site in Albania.
sum: Butrint is an ancient city on a lake near the southern tip of Albania, facing Corfu, inhabited from the Greek period through Roman, Byzantine and Venetian times until it was abandoned in the late Middle Ages.
